CBD2 of CALX1 is structurally distinct from the mammalian NCX-CBD2 and the alternative splicing variation of CBD2 can modulate its Ca(2+) affinity.

the structural basis for diverse Ca(2+) interactions with NCX isoforms is the result of a combination of local structural variations of Ca(2+ binding sites in CBD2 and alternative splicing modification of the protein domain-domain arrangement.
the structural diversity of NCX proteins is a major determinant for their Ca(2+) sensing and regulation.
